extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication; automated scaffold claims were replaced with paper-specific Ar-1 membrane and resistance evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Ar-1 is the best-supported antibacterial lead in this paper because Table 1 shows low MIC50/MIC90 values against both M. abscessus morphotypes while Tables 2 and 3 show lower host-cell and erythrocyte toxicity than most other tested arenicins.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Ar-1 compared with arenicin and Abu derivatives
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is an activity/safety prioritization claim, not a molecular mechanism by itself.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: For Ar-1, the paper directly supports a membrane-directed mechanism in M. abscessus using propidium iodide membrane permeabilization, lipid monolayer insertion, and scanning electron microscopy morphology assays.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Ar-1 against M. abscessus S and R variants
direct_assay_types: scanning electron microscopy after Ar-1 treatment
mechanism_claims.limitations: The direct mechanism evidence is specific to Ar-1 and should not be generalized to every arenicin derivative.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The 42-day repeated MIC assay supports no detectable resistance development to Ar-1 under the tested in vitro conditions, contrasted with clarithromycin control behavior.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Ar-1 against M. abscessus S and R variants
direct_assay_types: serial passage repeated MIC determination over 42 days
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is an in vitro resistance-selection result and not evidence for clinical resistance prevention.
